profileEvidence.author: C
profileEvidence.summary: The historical Welsh Hillman worked as an upland sheepdog in Wales. It belonged to a regional pastoral tradition alongside the Welsh Grey and Black and Tan valley dog. Never listed by the Kennel Club, it was one of the local working types that sat behind the Border Collie name.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: An upland sheep worker from Wales’s regional pastoral tradition, the historical Hillman belonged to a wider range of local herding types.
